# Search generative AI control

*Feature* · also written generative AI control

A Search Console property setting (inherit, include or exclude) that controls whether a site appears in Google's generative AI features without changing its web rankings.

**Glossary** (*Search generative AI control*): A Search Console property setting (inherit, include or exclude) that controls whether a site appears in AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover, without affecting web rankings.

Narrative: the topic [The generative AI opt-out in Search Console](../topics/genai-optout.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

6 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 4 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 1 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en).

- [`D1-C030`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Docs: The Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI features in Discover. Excluding removes both links to the site and use of its content to ground answers. `[D1-C030, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C102`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: John Mueller's slide said Search Console has very few indexing-like settings and listed the Search generative AI control as the one control in his talk that is not a meta tag. `[D2-C102, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C103`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Setting the Search generative AI control in Search Console to exclude keeps a site's links and content out of Search generative AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode, so the site gets no traffic or impressions from them; include is the default. `[D2-C103, slide, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C196`](../sessions/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: Google said Search Console's generative AI reporting launched alongside the generative AI control, starting with impressions only, and may expand later. `[D1-C196, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C412`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's Search Console talk at the Deep Dive covered five Search Console launches of the past year: query groups, AI-powered configuration of the Performance report, generative AI control and reporting, platform properties for social accounts, and multimodal search reporting. `[D3-C412, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C067`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: nofollow is a link-graph hint for search engines, not an access control: to keep AI crawlers away from content, use robots.txt rules for the specific crawlers; at Google, Google-Extended covers Gemini training and grounding, and the Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews and AI Mode. `[D2-C067, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-IDX-10` **MAY** · Documented: Use the Search generative AI setting in Search Console only to take a property out of AI Overviews and AI Mode (2 of its claims mention it)
